# Architecture & API Requirements Quality Checklist: Backend Service Architecture and Reliability

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements in spec.md for the service layer, boundary validation, error handling, and dependency consolidation are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-08-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the allowed enum values for relationship `type` and `status` defined at the requirement level, not only referenced as "valid enum values"? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the specific HTTP status codes for each error category defined, rather than only "appropriate status categories"? [Gap, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the "referenced members must exist" rule specified for event creation as well as relationships (events carry member ids)? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the specific database clients considered "unused/redundant" identified so "single client" is verifiable? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for validating path/query parameters (e.g., non-numeric `:id`) at the boundary, not just request bodies? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]

## Requirement Clarity & Measurability

- [ ] CHK006 Is "duplicate equivalent relationship" defined by which fields constitute equivalence? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK007 Can "MUST NOT expose sensitive internal detail" be objectively verified — is "sensitive internal detail" defined? [Measurability, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "no observable behavior change for the client" anchored to a concrete per-endpoint contract baseline (status + body)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the boundary between "transport concerns" and "business logic" delineated clearly enough to test the separation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "clear domain errors" specified with expectations for message content? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Is the preserved `{ message, error? }` body (FR-001) consistent with "consistent error response shape across all endpoints" given some current responses omit `error`? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK012 Are the FR-006 domain rules consistent with the clarified deferral of complex genealogy (no contradictory expectations elsewhere)? [Consistency, Spec §Clarifications/§FR-006]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements defined and measurable for concurrent failing requests each receiving an independent, consistent response? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the recovery requirement — server keeps serving after a handled error — stated with an objectively verifiable criterion? [Recovery, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the rule-parity requirement (same rejection via API or direct service call) specified measurably? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements defined for the impact of removing an unused dependency on the retained client's behavior? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK017 Is the assumption that existing Zod schemas suffice for boundary validation validated? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the coordination with the planned accounts/collaboration feature (shared database client for sessions) captured as a documented dependency rather than left implicit? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
